reviewerIndependence: Authored only security probes/reports; product and deployment recipe authored by other agents
reviewedScope: New activity_read_store.py: owner validation, accepted store classes, fixed placeholders, one owner-correlated latest-session SELECT, bounded status enum and suppression of closed/unknown session links
api_history: unchanged signed-header authentication and owner source; additive activity-reader call and public state projection; no per-row provider/session/action polling
historyStatus/renderHistoryOrders: pending-only closed-session label/advice, receipt/order precedence and stale-link suppression with unchanged support/evidence/deadline behavior
Independent full review of deploy/e4_activity_session_rollout.py, its tests, manifest/preflight/rehearsal and explicit partial-publication rollback behavior
Final primary tests, real isolated PostgreSQL and exact retained-live dependency rehearsals, browser report/cleanup and redacted staged scan
conclusions: The signed Telegram subject is the sole history owner. Query user_id or foreign session proof cannot switch owners; invalid owners are rejected before SQL.
The latest session is selected by highest id within the same owner-scoped SQL statement as its order and link. Older active rows cannot revive a closed or unknown latest session.

Failed and expired metadata describe session closure only. Missing, null and unrecognized status remain unknown without a link; no payment, refund, order-failure or network-finality claim is inferred.

Receipt-sent, paid/sent and terminal order status retain precedence. The new closure advice is a constant string and still suppresses a stale closed-session link supplied by an inconsistent client row.
The new reader reuses configured connection authority; it adds no provider request, writer, credential, permission, dependency, polling or automatic retry.
A separate reader avoids publishing unrelated checkout drift into the shared bot repository. Compatibility with the exact preserved live helper is independently evidenced.
The deployment recipe publishes only module/main/HTML, preserves the shared repository hash, retains fsynced byte/metadata preimages, restarts Relay only and prohibits blind replay after uncertainty.
Rollback retains the additive module until old main has been restored and Relay restarted. Independent probes restored all partial states and a submitted-restart/lost-acknowledgement state exactly.
Autopilot remains failed with MainPID zero; this reviewer performed no production/customer reads, mutations, service restarts, provider calls or network probes.

limitations: This is an activity-only security/diff and deployment-recipe review, not a full application audit or full E4 acceptance.
Synthetic fixtures and public unauthenticated probes do not prove actual customer incidence, payment outcomes, human comprehension, Telegram/iOS/WebKit or screen-reader behavior.
Production readiness of authenticated SQL is supported by exact-byte isolated rehearsals; no live customer query was executed by the reviewer.
Routine authorized Relay restart resumes existing enabled payment/notification workers. This review does not claim their existing effects are disabled or zero.
Deployment remains the primary operator action; runtime application/post-deploy verification are not claimed by this pre-deploy gate.
